title: BMW to source battery cells from LGES and Samsung SDI - electrive.com
content:
BMW is expanding its regional network for battery cell supply. For the Gen6 batteries of the Neue Klasse, two additional suppliers, Samsung SDI in Europe and LG Energy Solution (LGES) in the USA, are coming onboard as the automaker aims to further regionalise its supply chains and secure supply.
Image: BMW
The BMW Group is expanding its supplier network for battery cells, with a stronger focus on regional sourcing. For the
sixth-generation high-voltage batteries (Gen6)
, which is destined for the electric models of the
Neue Klasse
, the automaker has begun engaging additional suppliers. Samsung SDI will supply BMW from its existing European plants in the future, while LG Energy Solution (LGES) will take on this role in the USA. Deliveries are expected to begin at the end of the 2020s.
With these two new partnerships, BMW is pursuing the “local for local” principle. The company aims to source components in the same regions where its vehicles are produced. This approach is intended to shorten transport routes, strengthen regional value creation, and enhance supply security. At the same time, BMW continues to rely on a globally diversified supplier network to avoid dependencies on individual manufacturers and markets.
“Diversifying procurement is an integral part of the BMW Group’s purchasing strategy,” explained Nicolai Martin, Board Member for Purchasing and Supplier Network, adding: “Through our battery cell partnerships, we are actively strengthening value creation in Europe and the US.”
Three cell suppliers for Europe; LGES in the US
In future, BMW will thus source battery cells from three European manufacturers: CATL, EVE Energy, and Samsung SDI. Meanwhile, in the US, LG Energy Solution will fulfil this role. The respective suppliers are expected to produce cells as close as possible to BMW’s battery and vehicle plants.
In line with this, EVE Energy has built a cell factory near BMW’s new plant
in Debrecen , Hungary
(DE), and CATL is currently ramping things up at a new factory
in Debrecen
in addition to its existing facility
in Arnstadt (Thuringia)
. Samsung SDI has long operated a plant in Göd, Hungary, where it was rumoured in 2023 that
46120-format cells for BMW would be produced in the future
. This now appears to be confirmed – at least indirectly, as BMW’s current press release does not specify either the cell format or the location used by the new supplier Samsung SDI. The new supplier for the US market, LGES, already operates several cell factories in the USA.
The assembly of Gen6 high-voltage batteries also follows this regional approach. BMW has established five new production sites near its vehicle plants:
Irlbach-Straßkirchen in Lower Bavaria
, Debrecen in Hungary,
Shenyang in China
, as well as
Woodruff in the USA
and San Luis Potosí in Mexico. The proximity between cell manufacturers, battery assembly, and vehicle production is intended to further stabilise supply chains.
Neue Klasse to feature different cell chemistries
The expansion of the supplier network coincides with a phase in which BMW is further diversifying its battery strategy. As reported, the Neue Klasse electric vehicles will not only use the initially planned NMC cells but will also
incorporate LFP batteries in the future
. BMW CEO Milan Nedeljković confirmed this during the Q3 earnings conference call. However, a comprehensive switch to LFP is not planned. Instead, BMW intends to decide on a case-by-case basis depending on the vehicle segment and use case. While LFP technology is more cost-effective, it also offers a different range, according to Nedeljković.
The Gen6 batteries are fundamentally based on large-format cylindrical cells with a diameter of 46 millimetres and two different heights: 95 and 120 millimetres. Compared to the previous prismatic NMC cells, BMW promises an energy density increase of around 20 per cent. The cells are integrated directly into the battery using the cell-to-pack principle. The battery housing, in turn, becomes part of the vehicle structure through the pack-to-open-body principle.
The current announcement does not specify which cell chemistries the two new suppliers, LGES and Samsung SDI, will provide for BMW. For now, the new partnerships should be understood as an expansion of the regional procurement base.
BMW also invests in its own battery expertise
In addition to external suppliers, BMW is expanding its own expertise in battery cell technology. Since 2019, the company has been researching new cell technologies at its
Battery Cell Competence Center in Munich
. Since 2022, the
Cell Manufacturing Competence Center in Parsdorf
has been studying near-series production processes. Additionally, since 2024, the
Cell Recycling Competence Center
in Salching has been working on its own direct recycling process to recover valuable raw materials and reintegrate them into the production process.
BMW emphasises that establishing regional battery ecosystems requires time, significant investment, and reliable framework conditions. In addition to attractive location conditions, implementable political guidelines are also crucial to enable the necessary industrialisation.

title: Used EV batteries marketplace Rebattex partners with LKQ Atracco - electrive.com
content:
Nordic companies Rebattex and LKQ Atracco plan to collaborate in the battery circular economy. Specifically, they intend to offer refurbished EV batteries from LKQ Atracco's locations in Sweden and Norway for sale via the Rebattex platform.
Image: Rebattex
Rebattex is a marketplace for used electric vehicle batteries, while LKQ Atracco specialises in vehicle parts and recycling. The two companies have now signed a framework agreement to resell suitable used batteries from LKQ Atracco’s workshops in Sweden and Norway. The collaboration aims to provide LKQ Atracco with access to potential buyers across Europe and “support transactions with structured battery information,” as stated in an accompanying announcement. Comprehensive documentation and traceability are mandatory for reselling batteries via Rebattex.
“Building a functioning market for used EV batteries takes more than bringing buyers and sellers together,” emphasised Rebattex CEO Andy Rietschel. “It requires trust, traceability, and clear information throughout the transaction. Our cooperation with LKQ Atracco is an important step towards making that market work in practice.”
Based in Stockholm, Rebattex describes itself as Europe’s B2B exchange and digital trading infrastructure for verified, used electric vehicle batteries. The company aims to make the evaluation, pricing, and trading of used EV batteries more transparent and easier for all parties involved.
Magnus Tagesson, CEO of LKQ Atracco, commented: “Used EV batteries are a valuable resource, and a stronger market can create more opportunities for them to be put to productive and circular reuse. We see potential in combining our experience in automotive recycling with REBATTEX’s dedicated platform for trusted battery transactions.”
The announcement does not specify the expected volume of battery sales. Instead, it states that the shared goal is to make suitable batteries “more accessible for repair, reuse and other suitable applications.” The agreement is intended to serve as a foundation for further developing the collaboration over time.

title: Posco Future M to supply 720,000 tonnes of battery materials to LG Energy Solution - electrive.com
content:
Posco Future M and LG Energy Solution are significantly expanding their collaboration on battery materials. Between 2027 and 2033, Posco Future M is set to supply a total of 720,000 tonnes of cathode and anode materials.
Image: Posco Future M
South Korean companies Posco Future M and LG Energy Solution (LGES) have signed a memorandum of understanding to expand their collaboration on battery materials. The agreement covers LFP cathode materials, synthetic graphite, ultra-high-nickel cathode materials, and future products such as sodium-ion battery materials and silicon anodes.
According to Posco Future M, the company will supply a total of 720,000 tonnes of cathode and anode materials to LGES over a seven-year period. The company has not specified how this quantity will be distributed among the individual material types. The partners intend to finalise a formal contract later this year.
The ramp-up for LFP is expected to be particularly rapid. Posco Future M plans to convert existing production lines for high-nickel cathode materials at its Pohang plant to LFP and begin supplying LGES from early 2027. The company states that some of the lines have already been retrofitted accordingly.
In the future, Posco Future M also intends to use a new process that utilises lithium sourced from the Argentine salt lakes of the Posco Group. This is expected to further reduce costs and secure supply more firmly within its own value chain.
Battery material deliveries to begin in early 2027
The two companies also aim to strengthen their collaboration on anode materials. Synthetic graphite will be produced in Korea and Vietnam and supplied to LGES. Posco Future M highlights its advantages in fast-charging capability and lifespan.
In addition, the MoU includes the joint development of future battery materials, such as those for sodium-ion batteries, ultra-high-nickel cathodes, and silicon anodes.
The partners also plan to deepen their cooperation on existing NCM deliveries. In the medium term, they aim to increase the proportion of metals recovered from used batteries. According to Posco Future M, this will improve cost efficiency while strengthening material cycles.
The cooperation also aims to better mitigate regulatory and geopolitical risks. Both companies intend to jointly respond to new requirements in key markets, such as stricter supply chain regulations in the USA and Europe. In
, both LG Energy Solution and Posco announced plans to delay and reprioritise battery investments due to weaker demand for electric vehicles. The new agreement therefore signals less of a return to blanket growth and more of a targeted investment in cell chemistries and materials that are gaining importance for more affordable electric vehicles, stationary storage, and future battery generations.
With the seven-year framework, Posco Future M and LG Energy Solution are significantly expanding their collaboration beyond traditional high-nickel materials. The rapid entry into LFP in particular demonstrates how strongly priorities in the battery industry are shifting.

Image: BMW

title: Trafigura signs 10-year lithium offtake agreement with EnergyX - Batteries News
content:
Trafigura signs 10-year lithium offtake agreement with EnergyX
Geneva, 12 October 2026
– Trafigura has signed a binding 10-year offtake agreement with Energy Exploration Technologies, Inc. (“EnergyX”) for 100,000 metric tons of battery-grade lithium products from its projects in the US and Chile.
Under the agreement, Trafigura will purchase lithium carbonate from EnergyX’s Project Black Giant in Antofagasta, Chile and lithium hydroxide from Project Lonestar in Texas, US. Trafigura has agreed to purchase 66% of Phase 1 offtake from Black Giant and 30% of Phase 1 offtake from Lonestar. A significant share of the volumes are expected to supply the US battery supply chain.
EnergyX produces lithium using its proprietary direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology. EnergyX is targeting commercial-scale production at Black Giant in 2028, and at Lonestar in 2029.
The agreement supports the bankability of both projects, with offtake being a key requirement for EnergyX’s financing from the U.S. EXIM Bank and additional project finance lenders.
Daniel von Arx,
Head of Battery Metals at Trafigura, said:
We are pleased to support EnergyX as it develops its lithium projects in Chile and the US.
”Long-term offtake is an important step in moving projects into production, and this agreement reflects our ability to help bring strategic critical minerals projects online and build secure, diversified supply chains. Drawing on our logistics network and market expertise, we look forward to supplying these battery-grade lithium products to customers, supporting supply chains for the US automotive and energy storage industries.”
Teague Egan,
Founder and CEO of EnergyX, said:
Offtake agreements are among the most important steps in taking a lithium project from development to production.
”A long-term purchase commitment from a counterparty of Trafigura’s scale and credit quality shows that the market wants EnergyX’s product. It also gives lenders and investors the revenue visibility they need before committing capital to commercial construction.”

title: BMW Group begins series production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries in Shenyang - Batteries News
content:
BMW Group begins series production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries in Shenyang
+++ Shenyang is the third location in the global Gen6 production network +++ Local production of high-voltage batteries for Neue Klasse models in China +++ New cylindrical cells deliver more than 20 percent higher energy density and up to 30 percent faster charging and greater range +++
Shenyang is the third location in the global Gen6 production network
Local production of high-voltage batteries for Neue Klasse models in China
New cylindrical cells deliver more than 20 percent higher energy density and up to 30 percent faster charging and greater range
Munich/Shenyang.
The BMW Group has begun series production of its Gen6 high-voltage batteries in Shenyang. Following Debrecen and Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Shenyang is the third location in the new global production network for Gen6 battery technology. The start of production in China marks another important milestone in the technology’s global industrialization. The high-voltage batteries produced locally will form the energy core of future Neue Klasse models built in China.
Dr. Raymond Wittmann,
member of the Board of Management of BMW AG responsible for Production, said:
The high-voltage battery is a key component of our all-electric vehicles and one of the BMW Group’s most important technologies for the future.
”The start of Gen6 battery production in China demonstrates how quickly and systematically we are industrializing our latest technology across our global production network. This creates a key prerequisite for the successful global ramp-up of the Neue Klasse. Production in Shenyang exemplifies our global approach: We manufacture locally, efficiently and close to our markets, in line with uniform global standards and the highest quality.”
Gen6 technology delivers substantial customer benefits
The Gen6 high-voltage battery represents a technological leap forward for the all-electric models of the Neue Klasse. Compared with the previous cell generation, the newly developed cylindrical cells offer more than 20 percent higher energy density. Charging speed and range increase by up to 30 percent.
This is made possible by the new cell-to-pack concept: The cylindrical cells are integrated directly into the battery housing, eliminating the conventional module level. This makes more efficient use of the available installation space and allows the high-voltage battery to be integrated flexibly into different vehicle models.
The Energy Master plays a key role. Developed by the BMW Group, this central control unit is located directly on the high-voltage battery and consolidates essential power-supply and battery-management functions.
Global production network for sixth-generation high-voltage batteries
The BMW Group is establishing a global production network for its sixth generation of high-voltage batteries. The batteries are manufactured close to the respective vehicle plants. This shortens transport routes, supports a stable supply and strengthens the resilience of the production network. Following Debrecen, Hungary, and Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Germany, Shenyang is the third location in the global network.
The battery assembly locations in Woodruff, USA, and San Luis Potosí, Mexico, will also begin series production in the coming months. Uniform production, quality and safety standards apply worldwide, while each location contributes its regional manufacturing and supplier expertise.
How the Gen6 high-voltage battery is produced
The battery cells are first inspected and then joined with the cooling units to form cell clusters. After laser cleaning, the cell clusters and cell contact system are precision-welded together. A specialized foaming process bonds the components into a single mechanical unit, contributing to the safety, stability and longevity of the high-voltage battery. The housing is then closed, sealed and riveted. In the final assembly step, the Energy Master is installed before each high-voltage battery undergoes a complete end-of-line test.
Digital processes ensure quality and reliability
Production of Gen6 high-voltage batteries combines high-precision manufacturing processes with end-to-end digital quality assurance. Production data is captured and analyzed throughout the entire process. Digital twins, data analytics and AI-supported inspection methods help detect deviations at an early stage and ensure traceability. Among other parameters, inline inspection systems monitor laser-welded joints in real time. At the end of the assembly process, every high-voltage battery undergoes comprehensive testing for quality, safety and functionality.
With local battery production, the BMW Group is strengthening its local-for-local strategy: Future technologies are industrialized close to the market and in accordance with uniform global standards—and manufactured where the vehicles are produced. This makes production and logistics more efficient and resilient.
Questions and answers
Why is the BMW Group producing Gen6 high-voltage batteries in Shenyang?
The batteries are manufactured where the vehicles are produced. Local production in Shenyang will supply future Neue Klasse models built in China, shorten transport routes and contribute to an efficient and resilient supply chain.
What role does Shenyang play in the global Gen6 production network?
Following Debrecen in Hungary and Irlbach-Straßkirchen in Germany, Shenyang is the third location in the global production network for Gen6 high-voltage batteries. Additional battery assembly locations in Woodruff, USA, and San Luis Potosí, Mexico, will begin series production in the coming months.
What does “local for local” mean in battery production?
“Local for local” means industrializing key future technologies close to the market and producing them near the respective vehicle plants. Uniform production, quality and safety standards apply worldwide, while each location contributes its regional manufacturing and supplier expertise.
What is the BMW Group’s Gen6 high-voltage battery?
The Gen6 high-voltage battery is the new battery generation for the all-electric models of the Neue Klasse. Newly developed cylindrical cells, the cell-to-pack concept and the Energy Master deliver a technological leap in energy density, charging speed, range and flexible integration into different vehicle models.
What are the benefits of Gen6 battery technology?
Compared with the previous cell generation, the new cylindrical cells offer more than 20 percent higher energy density. Charging speed and range increase by up to 30 percent. Integrating the cells directly into the battery housing also makes more efficient use of the available installation space.
What is the Energy Master?
The Energy Master is the central control unit for the Gen6 high-voltage battery developed by the BMW Group. It is located directly on the battery and consolidates essential power-supply and battery-management functions.
How does the BMW Group ensure the quality of Gen6 high-voltage batteries?
Production data is captured and analyzed throughout the entire manufacturing process. Digital twins, data analytics, AI-supported inspection methods and inline inspection systems help detect deviations at an early stage and ensure traceability. Finally, every high-voltage battery undergoes comprehensive testing for quality, safety and functionality.

title: Changan and CATL to collaborate on 1,500 km solid state cells, establish 75 GWh battery lines - Batteries News
content:
Changan and CATL to collaborate on 1,500 km solid state cells, establish 75 GWh battery lines
Chinese automaker
has officially announced plans to deepen its partnership with battery giant CATL. The two firms have committed to expanding joint battery production capacity to 75 GWh and collaborating on
solid-state batteries
(SSBs) and
sodium-ion cells
Like its previous statements on its in-house SSBs, Changan made its announcement on an interactive platform owned by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The automaker also expressed commitment to prospective industries, including humanoid robots and China’s “low-altitude economy”.
More cells with CATL
Changan and CATL are not new partners in China’s automotive sector, having established a joint venture (JV), CATL-Changan (时代长安, Times Changan), earlier in 2023. The JV supplies cells to Changan’s in-house NEV brands, including Avatr, Deepal, and Nevo.
, a Chinese battery industry outlet, reports that CATL-Changan is on track to reach 50 GWh of battery production capacity, a plan Changan revealed at an investor relations event in May 2025.
The announcement means CATL-Changan will receive an additional 25 GWh of capacity and new production lines. The JV plans to establish a 700,000-square-meter facility and invest 5 billion yuan (~750 million USD) in the expansion.
According to Changan, the new facility will integrate the “latest generation of CATL battery tech” and supply cells to the automaker’s NEV brands. It’s planned to start operations in 2027 and meet the 25 GWh goal in three years. It will be situated in a high-tech zone between Chongqing City and Sichuan Province.
The automaker expects the expansion to bring in annual revenue of 10 billion yuan (~1.5 billion USD), create 2,500 jobs, and generate 300 million yuan (~45 million USD) in tax revenue for the local community.
Changan may also see this move as a way to cut costs.
ZAKER News
, a Chinese automotive outlet, reports that the Chongqing-based automaker is only earning 68 yuan (10 USD) per car, and is under heavy pressure to boost profits.
A JV with CATL would give it access to cheap in-house cells, and avoid high acquisition costs for battery packs,which is one of the priciest components in an NEV.
More on Changan’s SSBs
Changan has joined the race for SSBs in China, announcing its
Golden Bell
(Jinzhongzhao) cells in November 2023. The automaker says it’s aiming for an energy density of 400 Wh/kg and claims it will be 70% safer than rivals because it uses “AI remote diagnosis technology”.
It also claims the new Golden Bell cells will help EVs reach ranges over 1,500 km and says cell degradation won’t be noticeable for at least 600,000 km. Cell life will exceed 5,000 cycles, and Golden Bell packs will support 6C charging, enabling a 30-80% charge in 9 minutes.
The automaker has also reiterated its development schedule for the Golden Bell cells, aiming for vehicle road tests in 2026 and ramping up to commercial production in 2027.

title: NOVONIX Achieves ISO 9001 Quality Management Certification - Batteries News

NOVONIX Achieves ISO 9001 Quality Management Certification
CHATTANOOGA, Tenn., Oct. 07, 2026
(GLOBE NEWSWIRE)
— NOVONIX Limited (NASDAQ: NVX, ASX: NVX) (“NOVONIX” or the “Company”), a leading battery materials company, today announced that it has achieved certification to ISO 9001:2015
he internationally recognized standard for quality management systems.
ISO 9001 certification follows an independent assessment of NOVONIX’s quality management system and confirms that the Company has established and implemented processes and controls designed to consistently meet customer and applicable regulatory requirements and drive continual improvement.
ISO 9001 is the world’s most widely recognized quality management standard and is used across global manufacturing supply chains as an independent benchmark for quality management. For NOVONIX, certification represents an important milestone as the Company scales its Riverside facility in Chattanooga, Tennessee, for commercial production of high-performance synthetic graphite active anode material (AAM). Robust quality management systems are an important component of customer qualification, supplier approval, and ongoing commercial relationships with major battery cell manufacturers and other customers.
Mike O’Kronley,
Chief Executive Officer of NOVONIX, sai
Our customers require not only high-performance material, but confidence that we have the systems and discipline necessary to manufacture consistently and reliably at commercial scale,
Achieving ISO 9001 certification provides independent certification of the quality infrastructure we have built and reinforces our ability to serve customers as a reliable domestic supplier of high-performance synthetic graphite AAM.”
ISO 9001 certification complements, but does not replace, customer-specific product qualification requirements and provides a recognized quality management framework supporting customer qualification and commercial supply.
Meghan Vandelinder,
Senior Manager, Quality Control at NOVONIX, said:
ISO 9001 certification reflects the company-wide effort to embed quality into how we operate,
“The systems we have established to control our processes, measure performance and continuously improve are essential to meeting our customers’ demanding quality and consistency requirements.”
This announcement has been authorized for release by NOVONIX Chairman, Admiral Robert J. Natter, USN Ret.

HPQ Silicon Signs Cell Evaluation Agreement with Aptera Motors for HPQ ENDURA+ High-Capacity Battery Cells
MONTREAL, Canada
— HPQ Silicon Inc. (“HPQ” or the “Company”) (TSX-V: HPQ) (
OTCQB: HPQFF
FRA: 8PY1
), a technology company specializing in advanced materials innovation and the development of next-generation processes, is pleased to announce that HPQ Silicon, through its
HPQ ENDURA+
battery initiative, together with its French technology partner Novacium SAS (“Novacium”), has signed a Cell Evaluation and Confidentiality Agreement with
Aptera Motors Corp.
(“Aptera”) (NASDAQ:
), a Nasdaq-listed U.S. solar mobility company advancing ultra-efficient transportation.
Under the agreement, Aptera will evaluate HPQ ENDURA+ high-capacity 21700 lithium-ion cells based on Novacium’s silicon-based anode materials and related cell technology. The evaluation will include laboratory testing.
The agreement represents an important step in HPQ’s North American battery commercialization strategy, moving HPQ ENDURA+ cells from technology development and internal validation into application-level evaluation.
Advancing HPQ ENDURA+ Toward Commercial Applications
Aptera is developing a solar electric vehicle designed around ultra-high efficiency, aerodynamics and integrated solar generation. The company has recently reported several milestones, including receiving an EPA Certificate of Conformity for its 2026 Launch Edition and announcing a manufacturing partnership with Launch Design.
For HPQ, the evaluation provides an opportunity for ENDURA+ cells to be assessed in an application where energy density and overall system efficiency are important engineering considerations.
Bernard Tourillon
, President and CEO of HPQ Silicon, said:
This agreement represents exactly the kind of progression we have been working toward with HPQ ENDURA+,
“We have focused on moving our technology from advanced materials to high-performance cells, and ultimately into application-level evaluation, where its performance can be assessed in an EV application. We are excited to begin this process and see where the results may lead.”
Novacium has been advancing silicon-based anode materials and related cell technologies designed to increase the energy-storage capabilities of conventional lithium-ion battery formats. HPQ holds applicable commercial rights relating to Novacium technology in North America and participates in the commercial and industrial follow-up of potential future deployment.
Jed Kraiem,
Chief Operating Officer of Novacium SAS, said:
Moving into evaluation with Aptera is an important next step for our cell technology,
“Our development work has been focused on translating the performance of our silicon-based materials into practical, high-capacity cells. Having those cells evaluated provides valuable application-level feedback, and we look forward to supporting Aptera’s technical team throughout the process.”
The evaluation also marks another step in HPQ’s strategy of building a North American commercialization pathway for HPQ ENDURA+, advancing from technical development into application-level evaluation as a first step toward validation for EV applications.
The initial evaluation does not constitute a commercial supply commitment. If the results support continued discussions, the parties may separately consider subsequent technical, qualification and commercial steps.

title: Schrödinger Research Published in Nature Reveals New Insights into Lithium-Ion Battery Chemistry - Batteries News
content:
Schrödinger Research Published in Nature Reveals New Insights into Lithium-Ion Battery Chemistry
New study uncovers multi-lithium ion clustering in common battery electrolytes, paving the way for improved battery performance and design
NEW YORK–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Schrödinger, Inc. (Nasdaq: SDGR) today announced the publication of new research in
that reveals critical insights into the atomic-scale structure of lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrolytes. In a joint study with researchers from Columbia University and the New York Structural Biology Center, the team discovered new insights that challenge long-held assumptions of the fundamental chemistry of lithium-ion batteries, including multi-lithium ion complexes that may play an important role in electrolyte behavior and battery function. These new mechanistic insights into electrolyte behavior have the potential to transform battery development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive design to high-throughput, rational, computationally-driven design for higher-capacity, faster-charging, and longer-lasting batteries.
The research, which leveraged Schrödinger’s physics-powered computational platform, addresses a long-standing bottleneck in energy storage design. LIB electrolytes are crucial for battery performance, influencing properties such as conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation, and electrochemical stability. LIB electrolytes also drive the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase, which is the critical protective film on the battery anode that dictates battery lifespan and safety. However, a detailed atomic-level understanding of how electrolyte structure impacts these properties had remained limited. Utilizing Schrödinger’s advanced machine learning force field technology, the team simulated LIB electrolytes at unprecedented accuracy and scale. These simulations showed that lithium ions frequently form clusters coordinated by ethylene carbonate solvent molecules without the presence of anions, a fundamental structural phenomenon previously unrecognized.
Mat Halls,
senior vice president, materials science, of Schrödinger, stated:
Simulating complex battery systems has historically forced scientists to choose between quantum precision and large-scale simulation. Our machine learning force field technology eliminates that trade-off,
“Predicting these multi-lithium complexes and validating them experimentally demonstrates that our platform can detect previously inaccessible chemical phenomena to accelerate materials discovery.”
Richard Friesner,
co-founder and member of the Board of Directors at Schrödinger, and William P. Schweitzer Professor of Chemistry at Columbia University, stated:
Using Schrödinger’s proprietary, advanced machine learning force fields, we discovered lithium ions in batteries actually group together into clusters in the absence of anions, and that these clusters are what drive the creation of the protective film on the battery’s surface,
“Predicting this unexpected chemistry computationally and confirming it experimentally demonstrates that Schrödinger’s physics-powered platform can accurately model the hidden atomic details of batteries. Furthermore, these results suggest that many, if not most, complex chemical systems are now amenable to predictive physics-based simulation using machine learning force fields to atomic resolution.”
Key Findings:
Multi-Lithium Ion Clustering: In standard battery electrolytes, up to 40% of lithium ions group together into multi-ion clusters, with clustering becoming even more prevalent at higher salt concentrations. This finding upends the long-held assumption that lithium ions remain predominantly isolated in solution.
Accurate Experimental Validation: The machine learning force field simulations demonstrate strong agreement with a wide range of condensed-phase experimental data, including NMR spectra, electrolyte density, viscosity, ionic conductivity, and diffusion coefficients, confirming the physical reality of the predicted multi-lithium clusters.
Electrochemical Implications: Quantum chemical calculations indicate that these multi-lithium clusters have uniquely facile reduction potentials, suggesting they are key intermediates in the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase, which is critical for battery longevity and safety.
Foundation for Rational Electrolyte Design: The insights gained provide a fundamental understanding that can guide the rational design of next-generation electrolytes with enhanced performance, stability, and charge rates.

content:
Varroc and Forsee Power to Form Joint Venture to Scale EV Battery Solutions in India
Varroc to exercise management and operational control, strengthening its position in India’s evolving electric mobility ecosystem
PUNE, India–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Regulatory News:
As electric mobility gathers momentum across the world, the automotive industry is entering a new phase of transformation- one that calls for technology solutions that can evolve with changing vehicle architectures, customer requirements and the growing scale of electrification. In India, this transition presents a significant opportunity to build scalable, cost-effective and application-specific solutions that support OEMs across an expanding range of vehicle segments.
Recognising this evolving landscape,
Varroc Engineering Limited (VARROC| 541578 | INE665L01035),
a global automotive technology company, and
Forsee Power (FR0014005SB3 – ALFOR),
a specialist in smart battery systems, to enter into a joint venture to expand their electric mobility portfolio and combine their complementary capabilities to developadvanced battery-pack solutions.
As part of the transaction, Varroc will acquire a 45% equity stake in Forsee Power India, Forsee Power’s Indian subsidiary focused on battery-pack systems and exercise management and operational control on the entity. The joint venture is proposed to operate in India subject to applicable regulatory and corporate approvals. Varroc will also subscribe to Optionally Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares (OCPRS) to support the joint venture.
The joint venture will initially focus on battery packs for three-wheelers, with a roadmap to address two-wheelers, light commercial vehicles, buses, trucks, off-highway and industrial vehicles.
Commenting on the partnership,
Arjun Jain,
Whole Time Director & CEO – Business I, Varroc, said
Electric mobility is both evolving and growing rapidly, thus creating new opportunities and new requirements for the automotive industry.
”Through this evolution we believe OEMs will need partners who can anticipate changes and translate them into reliable, cost-effective solutions at scale. Our partnership with Forsee Power brings together complementary strengths in battery-system technology, automotive engineering, manufacturing and customer relationships. It represents an important step in expanding Varroc’s portfolio to address the evolving needs of our market and the future of mobility. This will further enhance addressable content per electric vehicle in all the segment.”
Highlighted Christophe Gurtner,
Chairman and CEO of Forsee Power,
With the rapid growth of electric mobility adoption in India, the opportunity is clear and we are ready to scale.
”Joining forces with Varroc combines our battery technology with local industrial strength and customer access. Three-wheelers are our starting point, with a clear ambition to expand across two-wheeler, commercial and industrial vehicles”
Forsee Power India brings established expertise in battery-pack technology and systems, while Varroc contributes automotive engineering capabilities, established OEM relationships and cost-effective, world-class manufacturing expertise.
Together, the companies aim to combine these strengths to develop battery-pack solutions adaptable to different vehicle architectures and operating conditions, while building the capabilities required to support the continued evolution and scale of electric mobility.
The joint venture reinforces Varroc’s commitment to anticipating the future of mobility, expanding its technology portfolio and supporting OEMs with solutions that enable safe, smart and sustainable mobility.

title: Texas Tech University and Caprock CEO Jonathan Grammer File For Ground-Breaking US Patent on Lithium Extraction from Produced Water - Batteries News
content:
Texas Tech University and Caprock CEO Jonathan Grammer File For Ground-Breaking US Patent on Lithium Extraction from Produced Water
AUSTIN, Texas–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Austin-based Caprock Direct Lithium Extraction (Caprock DLE) announced that it has exclusively licensed, for use in the oil and gas industry, a polymer-based lithium extraction technology co-owned by Texas Tech University and Caprock DLE CEO Jonathan Grammer.
The technology was developed through research at Texas Tech focused on extracting lithium from oil and gas produced-water streams. In 2024, Caprock DLE began funding Texas Tech research into lithium separation from produced water through the Critical Minerals and Produced Water Research Fund.
This is a historic step forward not only for the State of Texas and Texas Tech University, but also for the nation,
“With rising dependence on foreign lithium and growing domestic demand for battery energy storage, electric vehicles, phones, and laptops, the ability to recover lithium from produced water eases a major burden for oil and gas operators and strengthens U.S. critical-minerals security.”
Caprock DLE plans to integrate the licensed technology with its own proprietary technology as it develops a modular system for field deployment. The company began construction of its first modular unit this summer and plans to begin field operations in spring 2027.
Jennifer Souter,
Senior Managing Director for Research Commercialization, Texas Tech University, said:
The partnership with Caprock DLE exemplifies how universities and industry can work together to transform research discoveries into technologies with meaningful market potential,
“By protecting and licensing intellectual property developed through collaborative research, Texas Tech is helping move innovations beyond the laboratory and into applications that support domestic energy security, resource recovery, and economic growth.”
In March 2025, President Donald Trump signed executive actions intended to increase domestic mining and processing of critical minerals such as lithium and reduce U.S. reliance on foreign sources. As of early September 2026, battery-grade lithium carbonate was assessed near $19,750 per metric ton (CIF Asia). Texas produces more than 25 million barrels of produced water per day through normal oil and gas operations, costing operators upward of $10 billion per year. Recovering valuable critical minerals from those waste streams could create a domestic supply opportunity while potentially offsetting some disposal costs.
Raina Hornaday
, Co-Founder of Caprock DLE, said:
Working with Texas Tech on this research has been one of the most rewarding partnerships of my career as an alum,
“Partnering with Dean Tosha Dupras and the Texas Produced Water Consortium to turn a produced-water challenge into a domestic lithium opportunity is exactly why staying connected to Texas Tech matters.”
Dean Tosha Dupras,
This partnership represents the College of Arts & Sciences at its very best—bringing together innovative research, industry collaboration, and the talents of our alumni to address consequential challenges facing Texas and the nation.
” It is especially rewarding to see two of our alumni return as industry partners, combining their entrepreneurial vision with Texas Tech research to turn a costly waste stream into a potential domestic source of critical minerals.”
Separately, in June, Caprock DLE independently filed for patent protection on its proprietary modular unit. The company plans to integrate the Texas Tech co-owned, licensed technology with its proprietary technology in a system designed for deployment across Texas to recover lithium carbonate from produced-water streams.
According to Caprock DLE, its process has also shown success removing sodium and sodium chlorides. The company believes that capability could support treatment of produced water for potential reuse, including as cooling water for data centers.

title: Sunwoda Digital Battery Passport Solution Among Finalists at 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards - Batteries News
content:
Sunwoda Digital Battery Passport Solution Among Finalists at 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards
LONDON, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — The 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards ceremony took place in London today, with Wang Qiao, General Manager of Sunwoda Hungary, attending on behalf of the company. Sunwoda’s Digital Battery Passport Solution was among the nine finalists in the Supply Chain & Scope 3 Decarbonisation Project of the Year category.
Organised by UK sustainability media platform edie, the category recognises value-chain decarbonisation through supplier engagement, procurement and improved data. Other finalists included Prologis and Mobilityways’ Green Travel Programme, Syngenta’s Collaborative Carbon Reduction and HH Global’s Sustainable Procurement Framework. Sunwoda brought a battery lifecycle data solution to this cross-sector field.
The solution links battery value-chain data to support product carbon footprint management and sustainability disclosures. Battery data spanning raw material sourcing, manufacturing, use and recycling is dispersed among suppliers, manufacturers and downstream partners, complicating carbon accounting and traceability. Sunwoda’s solution links product identity, carbon footprint and compliance information in one digital record. This supports emissions hotspot identification, supply-chain coordination and product sustainability disclosure preparation.
Development began in 2023, with collaborative pilots in 2024 and the platform’s launch in October 2025. Six modules cover supply chain management, traceability mapping, product carbon footprint, due diligence, passport management and operational management. Covering 78 indicators, the platform integrates material sourcing, environmental performance and compliance records, helping partners collect and access information about the same battery product. Secure data exchange and permission-based access support collaboration while protecting data.
The platform has progressed to practical applications. In 2024, two battery passport projects jointly developed by Sunwoda and its partners were selected for the Global Battery Alliance’s Battery Passport pilot programme. According to edie’s project profile, Sunwoda completed five pilots in 2025 and engaged 28 key suppliers in carbon management.
Sunwoda has collaborated on battery passport development and applications with well-known domestic and international companies, including TÜV Rheinland and Siemens China. These collaborations build experience linking battery information across organisations and stages of use.

Saft Launches Production of France’s First Solid-State Batteries
Bordeaux, October 19, 2026
– Today, at its site in Bordeaux, TotalEnergies’ affiliate Saft will inaugurate new production lines for solid-state batteries* (those that use a solid electrolyte). Saft will be the first French manufacturer with the capacity to develop and produce solid-state batteries that use both sulfide and polymer electrolytes at room temperature, a technological combination with a wide range of applications.
Compact, safer, next-generation batteries
Solid-state batteries are seen as one of today’s most promising technologies. By replacing the traditional liquid electrolyte with a solid material, they offer increased safety in addition to energy density that is up to 50% higher than that of classic lithium-ion batteries.
They are produced using a dry electrode process, moreover, which is more environmentally responsible, cutting the CO2 emissions from this stage of production by up to 40%.
Concrete applications in aviation and space
The aim is to promote electrification in the aviation and space sectors, where gains in safety, performance and energy density are particularly valuable.
In aviation, Saft has already passed a first milestone, with the delivery of semi-solid state cells for the evaluation of future electric and hybrid aircraft architectures. Solid-state batteries have been identified as a technology that will be key to the electrification of aviation and have also attracted significant interest from the space industry.
Cedric Duclos
, Chief Executive Officer, Saft, said:
Solid-state batteries are among the most promising innovations for meeting tomorrow’s electrification needs.
These new production lines mark an important milestone for Saft, as we turn several years of research into real industrial capacity, a statement of our ambition to establish France and Europe as leading players in this strategic technology.

title: HPQ Silicon Partners with Open Markets to Scale Its Battery Business into a Standalone Company and Pursue a Listing on a Major US Exchange - Batteries News
content:
HPQ Silicon Partners with Open Markets to Scale Its Battery Business into a Standalone Company and Pursue a Listing on a Major US Exchange
The initiative’s main objective is to scale HPQ’s battery business into a standalone company (“NewCo”), with the following objectives, subject to definitive agreements, financing, and applicable approvals:
Securing third-party financing
for the North American battery business at the NewCo level, with the objective of reducing reliance on additional HPQ common share issuances;
Structuring a transaction that would provide HPQ with cash consideration, a majority retained equity interest in the new business, and a royalty on defined net revenue
, while maintaining HPQ shareholders’ indirect exposure to the future growth of the North American battery business;
Securing a full management and operations team
, including a CEO, CFO, CRO and Board of Directors
Evaluating strategic alternatives for NewCo
, including a potential future U.S. public listing, subject to financing, market conditions, and applicable regulatory and exchange requirements;
Focusing operational development and commercialization
of HPQ’s battery activities in North America through a standalone management team and board of directors;
Collaborating with the Open Markets team
Partners
collectively bring several decades of prior professional experience in investment banking and operational leadership at major financial institutions.
MONTREAL, Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — HPQ Silicon Inc. (“HPQ” or the “Company”) (TSX-V: HPQ, OTCQB: HPQFF, FRA: O08), a technology company specializing in advanced materials innovation and next-generation energy technologies, today announces that it has entered into a strategic consulting agreement (the “Agreement”) with Open Markets L.L.C-FZ (“Open Markets”) to assist with the proposed establishment and development of a dedicated North American battery business under the working name Project ENDURA.
The proposed U.S.-based corporation referred as “NewCo” has not yet been incorporated. The Agreement establishes the consulting mandate; the contemplated transfer of battery-related rights and commercial agreements and the proposed NewCo financing remain subject to definitive documentation, financing, required consents and applicable approvals.
Project ENDURA is intended to provide a dedicated corporate and operating platform through which HPQ’s North American battery activities can be developed, financed and commercialised.
The initiative is designed to bring together specified rights relating to HPQ’s North American battery activities with dedicated management, operating capabilities and the objective of securing third-party capital. HPQ and Open Markets intend to establish NewCo to finance, develop and operate the business and pursue its commercial objectives, with Open Markets expected to participate as a founding shareholder of NewCo. The scope of the rights and commercial agreements to be contributed, and the final ownership structure, remain subject to definitive documentation and applicable consents and approvals.
The parties are also evaluating capital markets alternatives for NewCo, including a potential future public listing in the United States, subject to market conditions, financing, applicable regulatory requirements and the execution of definitive agreements.
Capital strategy
To date, the development of HPQ’s battery activities has been funded principally at the parent company level. By establishing a dedicated, separately financed vehicle for its North American battery business, HPQ aims to fund commercialisation through third-party capital raised directly by NewCo, reducing reliance on additional HPQ common share issuances and the associated shareholder dilution.
Under the contemplated structure, HPQ would contribute certain North American battery-related rights and commercial agreements to NewCo in exchange for US$4.2 million in cash consideration and an expected 55% equity interest in NewCo following the initial financing.
The initial NewCo financing, currently targeted at approximately US$20 million, would fund the cash consideration payable to HPQ, an anticipated investment of at least US$8 million in production equipment and manufacturing capabilities, the recruitment of experienced industry executives and technical talent, as well as working capital and transaction-related expenses. These proposed allocations are preliminary and would depend on the financing proceeds available and NewCo’s final operating plan. The amount, structure and timing of the financing remain subject to market conditions and HPQ approval. No binding financing commitments have been secured as of the date of this release.
The transaction also contemplates a royalty to HPQ on defined NewCo net revenue.
HPQ would retain its equity interest in Novacium, its North American (Canada, Mexico and the United States) licences relating to Novacium’s clean-hydrogen activities, and its fumed silica project, all of which would remain outside the contemplated transaction. HPQ shareholders would therefore maintain their exposure to these activities while participating, through HPQ’s expected majority ownership of NewCo, in the commercial development of the North American battery business.
Governance and anticipated benefits
Management believes that establishing a separately financed and independently managed battery business could support the commercial development of HPQ’s North American battery activities and provide a dedicated platform for financing and operational execution. Under the contemplated governance structure, HPQ’s CEO would serve as Chairman of NewCo’s board, while responsibility for day-to-day operations, business execution and commercial development would rest with NewCo’s dedicated management team.
The contemplated transaction remains subject to definitive agreements, financing, required consents and approvals. All financing amounts and proposed transaction terms remain indicative and subject to change. There can be no assurance that NewCo will secure this financing or that HPQ will not require additional financing for its retained activities.
Commercial execution is the priority
Project ENDURA will initially focus on four areas:
Management:
recruiting a leadership team with the experience required to move the business from technology development to commercial operations.
Capital:
securing financing to build operating capacity and support growth without relying solely on HPQ parent company funding
Customers and partnerships:
developing commercial relationships with potential customers, strategic partners and industry participants across the North American battery market.
Operations:
establishing the production, supply chain and operating infrastructure required to support market entry and future scale.
Bernard Tourillon,
Chairman, President and CEO of HPQ Silicon, said:
We have made significant progress in developing our battery technologies.
”Our priority now is to turn that progress into a commercially operating business. Project ENDURA is designed to provide the dedicated leadership, manufacturing capabilities and capital needed to make that transition, with HPQ expected to hold a majority equity interest following the contemplated initial financing, subject to final terms,”
“This approach is intended to finance commercial development at the NewCo level, reducing the need for additional HPQ share issuances. Our immediate focus is execution: establishing production capabilities, developing customer relationships and building a sustainable business.”

Nano One estimates potential savings of up to US$1 million per year for every 1,000 tonnes per annum of capacity, based on SMM’s evaluation of One-Pot™
VANCOUVER, British Columbia–(
BUSINESS WIRE
Nano One® Materials Corp
. (“Nano One” or the “Company”)
(TSX: NANO) (OTCQB: NNOMF) (Frankfurt: LBMB)
, a process technology company specializing in lithium-ion battery cathode active materials, provides an update on its strategic collaboration with
Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.
(TSE: 5713) (“SMM”), a strategic project partner under
Nano One’s NRCan-funded programs
Since SMM’s strategic investment in 2023, the two companies have been closely collaborating on both technical and commercial aspects of the Company’s LFP cathode material production technology. The focus on LFP chemistry remains a key priority for this partnership, given the significant market opportunity as LFP continues its robust growth in volume and share of the lithium battery energy storage segment.
Munekazu Kawata,
Managing Executive Officer, General Manager of SMM’s Battery Materials Division said,
Our economic modelling of the One-Pot process continues to be positive, and we see it as a high-quality, cost-effective manufacturing solution for LFP cathode materials with potential from both a production and a commercial standpoint.
”Our customers have provided positive feedback on samples produced through the One-Pot process. We continue to advance our own LFP business, and our collaboration with Nano One is complementary to it as we work to serve growing demand for LFP.”
Continued Validation Work
SMM has continued to advance its validation work on the One-Pot process over the past year, including its own economic modelling, product testing and the supply of One-Pot LFP samples to its customers. This reflects SMM’s stated commitment to providing large, secure supplies of high-quality LFP cathode materials to markets around the world as demand grows. SMM continues to advance its existing LFP production and solid-phase process development while evaluating One-Pot as a complementary route to cost-competitive supply for its customers. Based on that modelling, Nano One estimates potential conversion cost savings of up to US$1 million per year for every 1,000 tonnes of annual capacity.
The positive customer feedback on One-Pot samples follows from that work and builds on the confidence in the One-Pot process that SMM
expressed in September 2025

COO of Nano One, said:
Sumitomo Metal Mining is a well-established producer with over two decades of experience in battery cathode materials.
”We are pleased that SMM sees the potential of our proprietary One-Pot technology from both a production and a commercial standpoint, and that their customers are responding positively to our samples. I believe this will further enhance the value proposition to potential customers, licensees and joint venture partners that we are engaging with. We are appreciative of the support and guidance that SMM has provided Nano One since their initial investment in the Company and are very pleased to see them advancing sampling of our One-Pot LFP with their own customers,”
Advancing Towards Commercial Supply
Nano One’s latest One-Pot LFP has reached a pressed density suitable for evaluation by high-performance cell producers and samples are ready for customer evaluation. Engagement with SMM’s existing cell manufacturing and automotive customers is underway. These are key steps in a multi-step product qualification pathway that must be completed in order to advance to eventual commercial offtake.
Strategic Collaboration
SMM and Nano One continue to work towards collaboration on a large-scale LFP production facility in Canada, subject to securing customer offtake, project financing and government funding support. SMM has participated as an in-kind project partner under the C$9.3 million NRCan Energy Innovation Program funding awarded to Nano One and has also been contributing technical expertise, testing and external validation as part of the C$3 million NRCan LFP supply chain initiative.

title: CATL unveils dual-battery system to accelerate heavy-duty truck electrification - Batteries News
content:
CATL unveils dual-battery system to accelerate heavy-duty truck electrification
CATL (HKEX: 3750) has unveiled a dual-electric range extension battery for heavy-duty
, pairing a swappable main battery with an independent on-board battery as it expands its push in freight electrification.
The world’s largest EV battery maker introduced the system in Beijing on Tuesday, alongside upgrades to its Qiji battery-swapping system aimed at reducing fleets’ energy replenishment and battery costs.
The system consists of 2 independent battery systems: a standardized, chassis-mounted swappable main battery and a 77-kWh range-extension battery behind the cab. The latter supports 3C charging and provides backup power.
Drivers of conventional battery-swapping trucks typically return to swap stations with about 30% charge remaining to avoid running out of power en route, leaving part of their leased battery capacity unused, CATL said.
With the backup battery, the system can increase the main battery’s depth of discharge (DOD) from about 70% to more than 95%, allowing trucks to return to a swap station with less than 5% charge remaining in the main battery.
The system can switch power delivery to the range-extension battery within milliseconds, maintaining uninterrupted power and providing redundancy under demanding operating conditions, the company said.
It uses what CATL calls a “1+X” architecture. The main battery remains standardized for compatibility with the Qiji swapping network, while the range-extension battery can be tailored to requirements such as low-temperature performance, high energy density or high power.
The 2 battery systems can be upgraded independently. The range-extension battery stays with the vehicle as an on-board asset, while the main battery can be leased flexibly according to seasonal freight demand, helping fleets reduce rental expenses during idle periods.
Alongside the new system, Qiji introduced the 260# and 300# standardized swappable batteries, with capacities of 432 kWh and 513 kWh, respectively, complementing its existing 75# battery.
The new-generation Qiji station can complete a battery swap in 5 minutes and reduces construction costs by 10%, CATL said. It requires no excavation pit and can be deployed in as little as 5 days.
The company also changed the billing method for its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) offering, charging customers for net energy charged rather than energy discharged, allowing them to retain the benefits of regenerative braking.
The change can reduce per-kWh battery rental costs for users on basic plans by up to 20%, further improving the economics of operating electric heavy-duty trucks, according to CATL.
The company plans to have 900 heavy-duty truck battery-swap stations operating by the end of 2026 and expand to 2,000 by 2027. Its long-term goal is to deploy 10,000 stations across China with partners.
Agreements covering 13,000 vehicles were signed at the event, with orders for battery-swapping products from major logistics companies including SF Holding and China Postal Express & Logistics.
The launch comes amid a rapid increase in new energy vehicle (NEV) penetration in China’s heavy-duty truck market. New energy heavy-duty trucks accounted for 50% of the segment in September, up from 29% a year earlier, according to China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) analysis of compulsory traffic insurance data.
CATL launched its Qiji Energy heavy-duty truck battery-swapping solution in June 2023 and introduced the 75# standardized swappable truck battery in May 2025, expanding its presence in logistics.
On June 30 this year, the company signed a strategic cooperation
agreement with J&T Express
to provide swappable batteries, swap-station equipment, and operation and maintenance services for more than 5,000 heavy-duty trucks.
Beyond the dual-electric range extension system, CATL also unveiled truck batteries for different transport applications, including ultra-light and ultra-thin packs mounted behind the cab, as well as chassis-mounted batteries for short-haul and long-haul operations.

title: South Korean top court finalizes 4-year sentence for battery maker CEO over deadly factory fire - Batteries News
content:
South Korean top court finalizes 4-year sentence for battery maker CEO over deadly factory fire
SEOUL – South Korea’s top court on Tuesday finalized a four-year prison sentence for Park Soon-kwan, chief executive officer (CEO) of lithium battery maker Aricell, over a deadly factory fire that claimed the lives of 23 workers in 2024.
The Supreme Court upheld the appellate court’s ruling, convicting Park of violating the Serious Accident Punishment Act by failing to fulfill his duties to ensure workplace safety.
The court also upheld a seven-year prison term for Park’s son, who served as Aricell’s chief operating officer, and a fine of 800 million won (about 602,000 US dollars) for the corporate entity.
The tragic disaster occurred on June 24, 2024, at an Aricell plant in Hwaseong, some 45 km south of Seoul. Lithium battery explosions triggered a massive blaze, leaving 23 workers dead and nine others injured.
A district court sentenced Park to 15 years in prison, marking the heaviest sentence since the Serious Accident Punishment Act took effect in 2022.
The appeals court, however, slashed the CEO’s prison term to four years, acquitting him of special charges regarding the installment and maintenance of emergency exit in each floor of the plant.

title: Viridi and Good Carbon Deploy One of the Largest Indoor Battery Energy Storage Systems in an Occupied US Residential Building - Batteries News
content:
Viridi and Good Carbon Deploy One of the Largest Indoor Battery Energy Storage Systems in an Occupied US Residential Building
BUFFALO, N.Y., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ —
, the industry leader in fail-safe distributed energy storage systems, and
Good Carbon Co.
, today announced the deployment of a 3.75MWh lithium-ion battery energy storage system (BESS) at
Peace Bridge Place
, a 105-unit affordable housing apartment building in Buffalo, New York. The project is one of the largest indoor lithium-ion battery systems in an occupied residential building in the United States.
At Peace Bridge Place, Viridi’s
RPSLinkIN indoor BESS
is part of a broader clean energy strategy that includes geothermal heating & cooling, domestic hot water, and high efficient building envelope upgrades. The 3.75 MWh system is designed to provide extended backup power for the fully electrified building during outages, while also helping reduce demand on the local grid during peak periods. Good Carbon Co., which focuses on revitalizing multifamily properties in communities throughout Western New York, selected the system to strengthen energy resilience for residents and enable the property to enable flexible, grid-responsive energy management.
Adam Serbert,
CEO of Good Carbon Co, said:
Energy is one of the biggest operating costs in multifamily housing, and how you manage it directly affects the long-term performance of a property
“At Peace Bridge Place, Viridi’s battery and energy management technology will help us reduce peak demand, avoid higher-cost periods and participate in demand response programs. That means lower operating costs, new revenue opportunities and a stronger economic foundation for keeping the property affordable and well maintained. For us, this is not just about one building — it is about creating a model we can apply across future multifamily projects.”
Viridi’s intelligent Energy Management System automatically stores and discharges electricity based on the needs of the fully electrified property and the local grid. It allows Peace Bridge Place to reduce electricity demand during peak periods and respond to utility signals when additional grid flexibility is needed, while providing greater energy resilience for residents. By reducing peak demand and participating in demand response programs, the system can help lower the property’s energy costs while creating new revenue opportunities.
New York State Energy Research and Development Agency
(NYSERDA) is providing support to Good Carbon Co. for the Peace Bridge Place project through its Future Grid Challenge. The Peace Bridge Place project is a
National Grid
pilot focused on integrating flexible, grid-responsive technologies into its distribution network. Viridi’s energy storage and energy management technology will work in coordination with
EnergyHub’s Edge Distributed Energy Resource Management System
(DERMS), enabling the property to respond to National Grid signals during periods of peak electricity demand.
Doreen M. Harris,
President and CEO, NYSERDA, said:
Peace Bridge Place demonstrates how forward-thinking energy storage solutions can ensure New York’s multifamily buildings are meeting the energy needs of its residents while creating a more reliable and resilient electric grid,
“Projects like this embody NYSERDA’s mission to spur innovation that drives New York toward a clean energy future.”
Distributed across seven battery rooms, the 3.75MWh system is integrated with Viridi’s proprietary Energy Management System (EMS), which optimizes the property’s electricity use while enabling it to respond to changing conditions on the local grid in two key ways:
Peak Shaving:
As the building’s grid energy draw approaches a monthly peak, the battery automatically discharges to keep demand below a target threshold, reducing peak demand and associated $/kW demand charges.
Seasonal Demand Response:
During peak events, National Grid dispatch signals are delivered through EnergyHub’s platform to Viridi’s energy management system, which then coordinates the response across the building’s battery and other energy systems
For participating residents, smart thermostat setpoints can be adjusted to “pre-cool” or “pre-heat” apartments before the event, enabling reduced HVAC consumption during the event while the battery discharges. Residents can opt out of individual events at any time. Together, these actions allow the property to reduce its net electricity demand while the local grid is under the greatest strain.
Deploying lithium-ion battery storage indoors at this scale requires rigorous safety standards. The risk of
thermal runaway
— and its potential to propagate from cell to cell — has historically constrained where lithium-ion systems can be installed. The RPSLinkIN system is designed to address that challenge through Viridi’s proprietary Fail-Safe Anti-Propagation architecture, a passive safety layer designed to prevent thermal runaway from spreading between cells.
That safety architecture has undergone industry-standard testing designed to evaluate how battery systems behave during a thermal runaway event. During
UL 9540A testing
, a cell was intentionally driven into thermal failure to determine whether the event would spread to surrounding cells. Viridi’s technology prevented cell-to-cell propagation, with no detectable release of heat, sparks, smoke, gas or flames. RPSLinkIN has also earned UL 9540 Listing from TÜV Rheinland, providing third-party certification of the complete energy storage system.
Jon M. Williams,
CEO of Viridi, said:
This project demonstrates what becomes possible when energy storage is designed to serve the building and the grid at the same time,
“Peace Bridge Place will now be able to reduce peak demand, respond when the grid needs support and strengthen resilience for the people who live there. The bigger opportunity is proving that large-scale lithium-ion storage can be safely integrated into the places where people actually live and work. By unlocking occupied buildings for energy storage, we can dramatically expand where distributed energy resources can play a role in strengthening the grid.”
Peace Bridge Place is also a proof point for Viridi’s ability to scale this technology beyond a single project. At its Buffalo manufacturing facility, the company currently has the capacity to produce approximately 400 MWh of battery systems annually — enough stored energy capacity to equal roughly one day of electricity use for 14,000 average U.S. homes. The facility also has room to expand production as demand grows.
The Peace Bridge Place project brings that broader vision into an occupied multifamily setting, combining fail-safe battery architecture, intelligent energy management and automated grid response to help lower operating costs, strengthen resilience and make the building a more flexible participant in the electric grid.

Hydrovolt and the Icelandic Recycling Fund to collaborate on end-of-life battery recycling solutions in Iceland
Hydrovolt enters collaboration agreement with the Icelandic Recycling Fund on end-of-life battery recycling solutions in Iceland. The agreement is part of Hydrovolt’s Nordic business strategy, ensuring no battery is ever wasted in the Nordic region.
The Icelandic Recycling Fund (IRF) executes the extended producer’s responsibility on certain goods, including EV batteries, in Iceland. It administers and distributes recycling fees, in accordance with The Act on Recycling Fees.
Íris Gunnarsdóttir,
Business Manager at the Icelandic Recycling Fund, says:
As battery volumes continue to grow, it is important that appropriate recycling solutions are in place.
”Through this collaboration with Hydrovolt, we are supporting the development of an efficient and responsible system for managing end-of-life batteries and recovering valuable raw materials,”
The total car park in Iceland consists of 17 percent electric and plug-in hybrids and has had a steady increase the last few years as the country is close to 80 percent electric of new cars sold. This requires Iceland to have solutions for handling battery waste in a sustainable and safe manner.
Hans Bjerkaas,
Chief Commercial and Development Officer, says:
We are thrilled to collaborate with IRF to offer safe and efficient handling of end-of-life volumes in Iceland.
”Through our logistics network and recycling process, we will ensure the recovery of critical raw materials from the batteries at high recovery rates,”
Hydrovolt offers a complete service offering for battery importers through reuse assessments and recycling of used batteries from electric vehicles and industrial applications. The company operates the Nordic region’s largest battery recycling facility in Norway with high safety standards and a total recycling rate close to 100 percent. The facility has a design capacity of 12,000 tonnes battery packs, in which equals 25.000-30.000 cars annually.
The collaboration agreement provides a basis for Hydrovolt to offer collection, transport and material recycling of batteries from electric vehicles and industrial applications in Iceland to its facility in Norway. Hydrovolt is already an approved treatment operator in Norway, Sweden and Denmark supporting producers and importers fulfilling their extended producer responsibility.

title: StellaON secures TÜV SÜD certification for Germany's medium, high and extra-high voltage grids - Batteries News
content:
StellaON secures TÜV SÜD certification for Germany’s medium, high and extra-high voltage grids
SHENZHEN, China, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — SINEXCEL (300693.SZ) has received TÜV SÜD unit certification for its StellaON 1250K/1575K power conversion systems (PCS), confirming compliance with Germany’s VDE-AR-N 4110, 4120 and 4130 standards. The certification covers medium-, high- and extra-high-voltage connections and supports the use of StellaON in utility-scale battery storage projects at different grid levels.
TÜV SÜD assessed the converters’ behaviour during grid faults, their active and reactive power control, and their response to frequency changes. The certification process combines FGW TR3 testing with TR4 simulation model validation under the TR8 programme. Engineers can use the validated DIgSILENT PowerFactory models to assess converter behaviour within a complete storage plant.
The three standards cover storage plants connected from distribution networks up to the transmission system. VDE-AR-N 4130 applies to networks at 220 kV and above, where connection requirements address the stability of the wider power system.
StellaON 1250K/1575K has black-start capability and reaches 98.5% efficiency at full load. It maintains rated output at ambient temperatures up to 55°C without derating and can deliver 1.5 times its rated power for up to 60 seconds. Variable-speed cooling keeps noise levels as low as 65 dB, allowing more flexibility when acoustic requirements limit equipment placement.
For developers and EPC contractors, the certificate supports PCS selection and the preparation of technical specifications for the relevant connection voltage. It also provides a basis for plant certification and connection approval. Project-specific design and network requirements remain subject to separate plant-level assessment.
StellaON has completed EU certification, as well as national certifications in Germany, Poland, Romania and other markets. It is listed for deployment in Romania, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. Certification is in progress in the United States, Spain, Austria and Chile, with completion planned by the end of 2026.
More than 15 StellaON projects in Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa are in system integration, delivery or on-site commissioning. Orders exceeded 500 MW in the first half of 2026. The PCS has also been validated in countries and regions including Vietnam and Myanmar, under extreme heat and humidity conditions and in island microgrid applications.
